```diff
+             raise ImportError("influxdb not available")
+         
+         with self.get_connection() as conn:
+             try:
+                 # Format points for InfluxDB

+                 for point in points:
+                     influx_point = {
+                         "measurement": measurement,
+                         "tags": tags or {},
+                         "time": point.pop("time", datetime.utcnow().isoformat()),
+                         "fields": point
+                     }
+                     influx_points.append(influx_point)

+                 conn.write_points(influx_points)
+             except Exception as e:

+                 raise

+     def create_table(self, table_name: str, columns: Dict[str, str], primary_key: Optional[str] = None,
+                     foreign_keys: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None, if_not_exists: bool = True) -> None:
+         """
+         Create a table in the database.
+         
+         Args:
+             table_name: Name of the table to create
+             columns: Dictionary mapping column names to their SQL types
+             primary_key: Name of the primary key column (if any)
+             foreign_keys: Dictionary mapping column names to referenced tables/columns
+             if_not_exists: Whether to add IF NOT EXISTS to the query
+         """
+         if self.db_type == DatabaseType.INFLUXDB:
+             logger.info("create_table not needed for InfluxDB, measurements are created automatically")
+             return
+         
+         # Build the CREATE TABLE query
+         query = f"CREATE TABLE {'IF NOT EXISTS ' if if_not_exists else ''}{table_name} ("
+         
+         # Add columns
+         column_defs = []
+         for col_name, col_type in columns.items():
+             if primary_key and col_name == primary_key:
+                 column_defs.append(f"{col_name} {col_type} PRIMARY KEY")
+             else:
+                 column_defs.append(f"{col_name} {col_type}")
+         
+         # Add foreign keys
+         if foreign_keys:
+             for col_name, reference in foreign_keys.items():
+                 column_defs.append(f"FOREIGN KEY ({col_name}) REFERENCES {reference}")
+         
+         query += ", ".join(column_defs) + ")"
+         
+         # Execute the query
+         self.execute_query(query)

+     def drop_table(self, table_name: str, if_exists: bool = True) -> None:

+             logger.info("drop_table not applicable for InfluxDB, use drop_measurement instead")
+             return
+         
+         query = f"DROP TABLE {'IF EXISTS ' if if_exists else ''}{table_name}"

+     def list_tables(self) -> List[str]:
+         """
+         List all tables in the database.
+         
+         Returns:
+             List of table names

+         if self.db_type == DatabaseType.SQLITE:
+             query = "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'"
+             results = self.execute_query(query)
+             return [row["name"] for row in results]
+         elif self.db_type == DatabaseType.POSTGRESQL:
+             query = "SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public'"
+             results = self.execute_query(query)
+             return [row["table_name"] for row in results]
+         elif self.db_type == DatabaseType.INFLUXDB:
+             with self.get_connection() as conn:

+                     return [m["name"] for m in measurements]
```

```diff
+ """
+ Cache Module
+ 
+ This module provides a caching system for storing frequently accessed data in memory,
+ improving performance by reducing database and network access.
+ 
+ Features:
+ - In-memory caching with configurable size limits
+ - Time-based expiration
+ - Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy
+ - Thread-safe operations
+ - Cache statistics and monitoring
+ """
+ 
+ import time
+ import logging
+ import threading
+ from typing import Dict, Any, Optional, List, Tuple, Callable, Union
+ from enum import Enum
+ from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+ import pandas as pd
+ import numpy as np
+ from collections import OrderedDict
+ 
+ # Import core utilities
+ from advanced_trading.core.config import get_config
+ from advanced_trading.core.common.serialization import serialize_to_json, deserialize_from_json
+ 
+ logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+ 
+ class CachePolicy(Enum):
+     """Cache eviction policies."""
+     LRU = "lru"  # Least Recently Used
+     LFU = "lfu"  # Least Frequently Used
+     FIFO = "fifo"  # First In, First Out
+     TTL = "ttl"  # Time To Live
+ 
+ class CacheEntry:
+     """
+     A single entry in the cache.
+     
+     Attributes:
+         key: The cache key
+         value: The cached value
+         created_at: When the entry was created
+         last_accessed: When the entry was last accessed
+         access_count: How many times the entry has been accessed
+         ttl: Time to live in seconds (None for no expiration)
+     """
+     
+     def __init__(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: Optional[int] = None):
+         """
+         Initialize a cache entry.
+         
+         Args:
+             key: The cache key
+             value: The value to cache
+             ttl: Time to live in seconds (None for no expiration)
+         """
+         self.key = key
+         self.value = value
+         self.created_at = time.time()
+         self.last_accessed = self.created_at
+         self.access_count = 0
+         self.ttl = ttl
+     
+     def access(self) -> None:
+         """Update access statistics when the entry is accessed."""
+         self.last_accessed = time.time()
+         self.access_count += 1
+     
+     def is_expired(self) -> bool:
+         """Check if the entry has expired."""
+         if self.ttl is None:
+             return False
+         return time.time() > self.created_at + self.ttl
+ 
+ class CacheStats:
+     """
+     Statistics for cache performance.
+     
+     Attributes:
+         hits: Number of cache hits
+         misses: Number of cache misses
+         evictions: Number of cache evictions
+         size: Current number of items in the cache
+         max_size: Maximum number of items allowed in the cache
+         created_at: When the cache was created
+     """
+     
+     def __init__(self, max_size: int):
+         """
+         Initialize cache statistics.
+         
+         Args:
+             max_size: Maximum number of items allowed in the cache
+         """
+         self.hits = 0
+         self.misses = 0
+         self.evictions = 0
+         self.size = 0
+         self.max_size = max_size
+         self.created_at = time.time()
+     
+     def hit(self) -> None:
+         """Record a cache hit."""
+         self.hits += 1
+     
+     def miss(self) -> None:
+         """Record a cache miss."""
+         self.misses += 1
+     
+     def eviction(self) -> None:
+         """Record a cache eviction."""
+         self.evictions += 1
+     
+     def update_size(self, size: int) -> None:
+         """Update the current cache size."""
+         self.size = size
+     
+     def hit_rate(self) -> float:
+         """Calculate the cache hit rate."""
+         total = self.hits + self.misses
+         if total == 0:
+             return 0.0
+         return self.hits / total
+     
+     def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+         """Convert statistics to a dictionary."""
+         return {
+             "hits": self.hits,
+             "misses": self.misses,
+             "evictions": self.evictions,
+             "size": self.size,
+             "max_size": self.max_size,
+             "hit_rate": self.hit_rate(),
+             "uptime": time.time() - self.created_at
+         }
+ 
+ class Cache:
+     """
+     In-memory cache with configurable eviction policies.
+     
+     This class provides a thread-safe cache for storing frequently accessed data

+     
+     Attributes:
+         name: Name of the cache
+         max_size: Maximum number of items allowed in the cache
+         policy: Eviction policy to use when the cache is full
+         default_ttl: Default time to live for cache entries (None for no expiration)
+         _cache: Dictionary of cache entries
+         _lock: Thread lock for thread safety
+         _stats: Cache statistics
+     """
+     
+     def __init__(self, name: str, max_size: int = 1000, policy: CachePolicy = CachePolicy.LRU,
+                 default_ttl: Optional[int] = None):
+         """
+         Initialize the cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             name: Name of the cache
+             max_size: Maximum number of items allowed in the cache
+             policy: Eviction policy to use when the cache is full
+             default_ttl: Default time to live for cache entries in seconds (None for no expiration)
+         """
+         self.name = name
+         self.max_size = max_size
+         self.policy = policy
+         self.default_ttl = default_ttl
+         
+         # Use OrderedDict for LRU and FIFO policies
+         self._cache = OrderedDict()
+         self._lock = threading.RLock()
+         self._stats = CacheStats(max_size)
+     
+     def get(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
+         """
+         Get a value from the cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             key: The cache key
+             default: Value to return if the key is not in the cache
+             
+         Returns:
+             The cached value, or default if the key is not in the cache
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             if key in self._cache:
+                 entry = self._cache[key]
+                 
+                 # Check if the entry has expired
+                 if entry.is_expired():
+                     self._remove_entry(key)
+                     self._stats.miss()
+                     return default
+                 
+                 # Update access statistics
+                 entry.access()
+                 
+                 # Move the entry to the end for LRU policy
+                 if self.policy == CachePolicy.LRU:
+                     self._cache.move_to_end(key)
+                 
+                 self._stats.hit()
+                 return entry.value
+             else:
+                 self._stats.miss()
+                 return default
+     
+     def set(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
+         """
+         Set a value in the cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             key: The cache key
+             value: The value to cache
+             ttl: Time to live in seconds (None to use the default)
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             # Use the default TTL if none is provided
+             if ttl is None:
+                 ttl = self.default_ttl
+             
+             # Check if we need to evict an entry
+             if key not in self._cache and len(self._cache) >= self.max_size:
+                 self._evict_entry()
+             
+             # Create a new entry
+             entry = CacheEntry(key, value, ttl)
+             
+             # Add the entry to the cache
+             self._cache[key] = entry
+             
+             # Move the entry to the end for LRU policy
+             if self.policy == CachePolicy.LRU:
+                 self._cache.move_to_end(key)
+             
+             # Update statistics
+             self._stats.update_size(len(self._cache))
+     
+     def delete(self, key: str) -> bool:
+         """
+         Delete a value from the cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             key: The cache key
+             
+         Returns:
+             True if the key was in the cache, False otherwise
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             if key in self._cache:
+                 self._remove_entry(key)
+                 return True
+             return False
+     
+     def clear(self) -> None:
+         """Clear all entries from the cache."""
+         with self._lock:
+             self._cache.clear()
+             self._stats.update_size(0)
+     
+     def exists(self, key: str) -> bool:
+         """
+         Check if a key exists in the cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             key: The cache key
+             
+         Returns:
+             True if the key is in the cache and not expired, False otherwise
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             if key in self._cache:
+                 entry = self._cache[key]
+                 if entry.is_expired():
+                     self._remove_entry(key)
+                     return False
+                 return True
+             return False
+     
+     def get_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+         """
+         Get cache statistics.
+         
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary of cache statistics
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             return self._stats.to_dict()
+     
+     def resize(self, max_size: int) -> None:
+         """
+         Resize the cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             max_size: New maximum size for the cache
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             # If the new size is smaller, evict entries until we're under the limit
+             while len(self._cache) > max_size:
+                 self._evict_entry()
+             
+             self.max_size = max_size
+             self._stats.max_size = max_size
+     
+     def _remove_entry(self, key: str) -> None:
+         """
+         Remove an entry from the cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             key: The cache key
+         """
+         del self._cache[key]
+         self._stats.update_size(len(self._cache))
+     
+     def _evict_entry(self) -> None:
+         """Evict an entry based on the cache policy."""
+         if not self._cache:
+             return
+         
+         if self.policy == CachePolicy.LRU:
+             # Evict the least recently used entry (first item in OrderedDict)
+             self._cache.popitem(last=False)
+         elif self.policy == CachePolicy.LFU:
+             # Evict the least frequently used entry
+             min_count = float('inf')
+             min_key = None
+             
+             for key, entry in self._cache.items():
+                 if entry.access_count < min_count:
+                     min_count = entry.access_count
+                     min_key = key
+             
+             if min_key:
+                 del self._cache[min_key]
+         elif self.policy == CachePolicy.FIFO:
+             # Evict the oldest entry (first item in OrderedDict)
+             self._cache.popitem(last=False)
+         elif self.policy == CachePolicy.TTL:
+             # Evict the entry closest to expiration
+             min_ttl = float('inf')
+             min_key = None
+             now = time.time()
+             
+             for key, entry in self._cache.items():
+                 if entry.ttl is not None:
+                     remaining = (entry.created_at + entry.ttl) - now
+                     if remaining < min_ttl:
+                         min_ttl = remaining
+                         min_key = key
+             
+             if min_key:
+                 del self._cache[min_key]
+             else:
+                 # If no entries have TTL, fall back to LRU
+                 self._cache.popitem(last=False)
+         
+         self._stats.eviction()
+         self._stats.update_size(len(self._cache))
+ 
+ class CacheManager:
+     """
+     Manager for multiple caches.
+     
+     This class provides a centralized interface for creating and accessing caches,
+     with support for different cache configurations and policies.
+     
+     Attributes:
+         _caches: Dictionary of caches
+         _lock: Thread lock for thread safety
+     """
+     
+     _instance = None
+     
+     def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
+         """Implement singleton pattern."""
+         if cls._instance is None:
+             cls._instance = super(CacheManager, cls).__new__(cls)
+             cls._instance._initialized = False
+         return cls._instance
+     
+     def __init__(self):
+         """Initialize the cache manager."""
+         # Only initialize once (singleton pattern)
+         if self._initialized:
+             return
+         
+         self._caches = {}
+         self._lock = threading.RLock()
+         self._initialized = True
+     
+     def get_cache(self, name: str, create_if_missing: bool = True) -> Optional[Cache]:
+         """
+         Get a cache by name.
+         
+         Args:
+             name: Name of the cache
+             create_if_missing: Whether to create the cache if it doesn't exist
+             
+         Returns:
+             The cache, or None if it doesn't exist and create_if_missing is False
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             if name in self._caches:
+                 return self._caches[name]
+             
+             if create_if_missing:
+                 # Get cache configuration from settings
+                 max_size = get_config(f"cache.{name}.max_size", 1000)
+                 policy_str = get_config(f"cache.{name}.policy", "lru")
+                 default_ttl = get_config(f"cache.{name}.default_ttl", None)
+                 
+                 try:
+                     policy = CachePolicy(policy_str)
+                 except ValueError:
+                     logger.warning(f"Unknown cache policy '{policy_str}', using LRU")
+                     policy = CachePolicy.LRU
+                 
+                 # Create the cache
+                 cache = Cache(name, max_size, policy, default_ttl)
+                 self._caches[name] = cache
+                 return cache
+             
+             return None
+     
+     def delete_cache(self, name: str) -> bool:
+         """
+         Delete a cache.
+         
+         Args:
+             name: Name of the cache
+             
+         Returns:
+             True if the cache was deleted, False if it didn't exist
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             if name in self._caches:
+                 del self._caches[name]
+                 return True
+             return False
+     
+     def clear_all_caches(self) -> None:
+         """Clear all caches."""
+         with self._lock:
+             for cache in self._caches.values():
+                 cache.clear()
+     
+     def get_all_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
+         """
+         Get statistics for all caches.
+         
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary mapping cache names to their statistics
+         """
+         with self._lock:
+             return {name: cache.get_stats() for name, cache in self._caches.items()}
+ 
+ # Singleton instance
+ _cache_manager = None
+ 
+ def get_cache_manager() -> CacheManager:
+     """
+     Get the singleton CacheManager instance.
+     
+     Returns:
+         The CacheManager instance
+     """
+     global _cache_manager
+     if _cache_manager is None:
+         _cache_manager = CacheManager()
+     return _cache_manager
+ 
+ def cache_data(key: str, value: Any, cache_name: str = "default", ttl: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
+     """
+     Cache data.
+     
+     Args:
+         key: The cache key
+         value: The value to cache
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to use
+         ttl: Time to live in seconds (None to use the default)
+     """
+     cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+     cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+     cache.set(key, value, ttl)
+ 
+ def get_cached_data(key: str, default: Any = None, cache_name: str = "default") -> Any:
+     """
+     Get cached data.
+     
+     Args:
+         key: The cache key
+         default: Value to return if the key is not in the cache
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to use
+         
+     Returns:
+         The cached value, or default if the key is not in the cache
+     """
+     cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+     cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+     return cache.get(key, default)
+ 
+ def clear_cache(cache_name: str = "default") -> None:
+     """
+     Clear a cache.
+     
+     Args:
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to clear
+     """
+     cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+     cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+     cache.clear()
+ 
+ def cache_exists(key: str, cache_name: str = "default") -> bool:
+     """
+     Check if a key exists in the cache.
+     
+     Args:
+         key: The cache key
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to check
+         
+     Returns:
+         True if the key is in the cache and not expired, False otherwise
+     """
+     cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+     cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+     return cache.exists(key)
+ 
+ def set_cache_policy(policy: Union[str, CachePolicy], cache_name: str = "default") -> None:
+     """
+     Set the eviction policy for a cache.
+     
+     Args:
+         policy: The eviction policy to use
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to modify
+     """
+     cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+     cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+     
+     if isinstance(policy, str):
+         try:
+             policy = CachePolicy(policy)
+         except ValueError:
+             logger.warning(f"Unknown cache policy '{policy}', using LRU")
+             policy = CachePolicy.LRU
+     
+     cache.policy = policy
+ 
+ def get_cache_stats(cache_name: str = "default") -> Dict[str, Any]:
+     """
+     Get cache statistics.
+     
+     Args:
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to get statistics for
+         
+     Returns:
+         Dictionary of cache statistics
+     """
+     cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+     cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+     return cache.get_stats()
+ 
+ def resize_cache(max_size: int, cache_name: str = "default") -> None:
+     """
+     Resize a cache.
+     
+     Args:
+         max_size: New maximum size for the cache
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to resize
+     """
+     cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+     cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+     cache.resize(max_size)
+ 
+ def cached(cache_name: str = "default", ttl: Optional[int] = None, key_fn: Optional[Callable] = None):
+     """
+     Decorator for caching function results.
+     
+     Args:
+         cache_name: Name of the cache to use
+         ttl: Time to live in seconds (None to use the default)
+         key_fn: Function to generate the cache key (defaults to function name and arguments)
+         
+     Returns:
+         Decorated function
+     """
+     def decorator(func):
+         def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
+             # Generate the cache key
+             if key_fn:
+                 key = key_fn(*args, **kwargs)
+             else:
+                 # Default key is function name and arguments
+                 key = f"{func.__name__}:{str(args)}:{str(kwargs)}"
+             
+             # Check if the result is cached
+             cache_manager = get_cache_manager()
+             cache = cache_manager.get_cache(cache_name)
+             result = cache.get(key)
+             
+             if result is not None:
+                 return result
+             
+             # Call the function and cache the result
+             result = func(*args, **kwargs)
+             cache.set(key, result, ttl)
+             
+             return result
+         return wrapper
+     return decorator 
```

```diff
+ """
+ Data Validation Module
+ 
+ This module provides tools for validating data against schemas, constraints, and integrity rules.
+ It helps ensure that data meets quality standards before being used for analysis or modeling.
+ """
+ 
+ import pandas as pd
+ import numpy as np
+ import json
+ import logging
+ from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union, Any, Tuple, Set, Callable
+ from enum import Enum
+ from dataclasses import dataclass
+ from datetime import datetime
+ 
+ # Import core validation utilities
+ from advanced_trading.core.common.validation import (
+     Validator, ValidationResult, ValidationError, validate_dict_schema
+ )
+ 
+ logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+ 
+ class ValidationSeverity(Enum):
+     """Severity levels for validation errors."""
+     INFO = "info"
+     WARNING = "warning"
+     ERROR = "error"
+     CRITICAL = "critical"
+ 
+ @dataclass
+ class DataValidationError:
+     """
+     Represents a data validation error.
+     
+     Attributes:
+         message: Description of the error
+         column: Column where the error occurred (if applicable)
+         row_index: Row index where the error occurred (if applicable)
+         severity: Severity level of the error
+         error_type: Type of validation error
+         details: Additional details about the error
+     """
+     message: str
+     column: Optional[str] = None
+     row_index: Optional[int] = None
+     severity: ValidationSeverity = ValidationSeverity.ERROR
+     error_type: str = "validation_error"
+     details: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
+ 
+ class DataValidationResult:
+     """
+     Result of a data validation operation.
+     
+     Attributes:
+         is_valid: Whether the data is valid
+         errors: List of validation errors
+         warnings: List of validation warnings
+         info: List of validation information messages
+         validation_time: When the validation was performed
+     """
+     
+     def __init__(self):
+         """Initialize a validation result."""
+         self.is_valid = True
+         self.errors: List[DataValidationError] = []
+         self.warnings: List[DataValidationError] = []
+         self.info: List[DataValidationError] = []
+         self.validation_time = datetime.now()
+     
+     def add_error(self, error: DataValidationError) -> None:
+         """
+         Add an error to the validation result.
+         
+         Args:
+             error: The validation error to add
+         """
+         if error.severity == ValidationSeverity.ERROR or error.severity == ValidationSeverity.CRITICAL:
+             self.errors.append(error)
+             self.is_valid = False
+         elif error.severity == ValidationSeverity.WARNING:
+             self.warnings.append(error)
+         elif error.severity == ValidationSeverity.INFO:
+             self.info.append(error)
+     
+     def merge(self, other: 'DataValidationResult') -> None:
+         """
+         Merge another validation result into this one.
+         
+         Args:
+             other: The validation result to merge
+         """
+         self.errors.extend(other.errors)
+         self.warnings.extend(other.warnings)
+         self.info.extend(other.info)
+         self.is_valid = self.is_valid and other.is_valid
+     
+     def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+         """
+         Convert the validation result to a dictionary.
+         
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary representation of the validation result
+         """
+         return {
+             "is_valid": self.is_valid,
+             "errors": [self._error_to_dict(e) for e in self.errors],
+             "warnings": [self._error_to_dict(e) for e in self.warnings],
+             "info": [self._error_to_dict(e) for e in self.info],
+             "validation_time": self.validation_time.isoformat(),
+             "error_count": len(self.errors),
+             "warning_count": len(self.warnings),
+             "info_count": len(self.info)
+         }
+     
+     def _error_to_dict(self, error: DataValidationError) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+         """Convert a validation error to a dictionary."""
+         result = {
+             "message": error.message,
+             "severity": error.severity.value,
+             "error_type": error.error_type
+         }
+         
+         if error.column is not None:
+             result["column"] = error.column
+         
+         if error.row_index is not None:
+             result["row_index"] = error.row_index
+         
+         if error.details is not None:
+             result["details"] = error.details
+         
+         return result
+     
+     def __bool__(self) -> bool:
+         """Return whether the data is valid."""
+         return self.is_valid
+ 
+ class DataValidator:
+     """
+     Validator for data quality.
+     
+     This class provides methods for validating data against schemas, constraints,
+     and integrity rules.
+     """
+     
+     def __init__(self):
+         """Initialize a data validator."""
+         self.validator = Validator()
+     
+     def validate_schema(self, data: pd.DataFrame, schema: Dict[str, Any]) -> DataValidationResult:
+         """
+         Validate a DataFrame against a schema.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to validate
+             schema: The schema to validate against
+                 The schema should be a dictionary mapping column names to their expected types
+                 and constraints.
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Validation result
+         """
+         result = DataValidationResult()
+         
+         # Check if all required columns are present
+         required_columns = [col for col, props in schema.items() if props.get("required", False)]
+         missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in data.columns]
+         
+         if missing_columns:
+             result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                 message=f"Missing required columns: {', '.join(missing_columns)}",
+                 error_type="missing_columns"
+             ))
+         
+         # Validate each column
+         for column, properties in schema.items():
+             if column not in data.columns:
+                 if properties.get("required", False):
+                     # Already reported above
+                     continue
+                 else:
+                     # Optional column is missing, add a warning
+                     result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                         message=f"Optional column '{column}' is missing",
+                         column=column,
+                         severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                         error_type="missing_column"
+                     ))
+                     continue
+             
+             # Validate column type
+             expected_type = properties.get("type")
+             if expected_type:
+                 self._validate_column_type(data, column, expected_type, result)
+             
+             # Validate column constraints
+             constraints = properties.get("constraints", {})
+             if constraints:
+                 self._validate_column_constraints(data, column, constraints, result)
+         
+         return result
+     
+     def _validate_column_type(self, data: pd.DataFrame, column: str, expected_type: str,
+                              result: DataValidationResult) -> None:
+         """
+         Validate the type of a column.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame containing the column
+             column: The name of the column to validate
+             expected_type: The expected type of the column
+             result: The validation result to update
+         """
+         # Map expected types to pandas/numpy types
+         type_map = {
+             "integer": (np.integer, int),
+             "number": (np.number, float, int),
+             "string": (str, object),
+             "boolean": (bool, np.bool_),
+             "datetime": (pd.Timestamp, np.datetime64),
+             "category": (pd.Categorical,),
+             "any": (object,)
+         }
+         
+         if expected_type not in type_map:
+             result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                 message=f"Unknown expected type '{expected_type}' for column '{column}'",
+                 column=column,
+                 severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                 error_type="unknown_type"
+             ))
+             return
+         
+         # Check if column type matches expected type
+         expected_types = type_map[expected_type]
+         
+         # Special case for datetime
+         if expected_type == "datetime":
+             try:
+                 # Try to convert to datetime
+                 pd.to_datetime(data[column])
+                 return
+             except:
+                 pass
+         
+         # Check if column type is compatible with expected type
+         column_type = data[column].dtype
+         type_compatible = False
+         
+         for t in expected_types:
+             if np.issubdtype(column_type, t) or column_type == t:
+                 type_compatible = True
+                 break
+         
+         if not type_compatible:
+             result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                 message=f"Column '{column}' has type '{column_type}', expected '{expected_type}'",
+                 column=column,
+                 error_type="type_mismatch"
+             ))
+     
+     def _validate_column_constraints(self, data: pd.DataFrame, column: str, constraints: Dict[str, Any],
+                                    result: DataValidationResult) -> None:
+         """
+         Validate constraints on a column.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame containing the column
+             column: The name of the column to validate
+             constraints: The constraints to validate against
+             result: The validation result to update
+         """
+         # Get column values
+         values = data[column]
+         
+         # Check for missing values
+         if constraints.get("required", False) and values.isna().any():
+             missing_count = values.isna().sum()
+             result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                 message=f"Column '{column}' has {missing_count} missing values, but is required",
+                 column=column,
+                 error_type="missing_values"
+             ))
+         
+         # Check for unique values
+         if constraints.get("unique", False) and not values.is_unique:
+             duplicate_count = len(values) - len(values.unique())
+             result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                 message=f"Column '{column}' has {duplicate_count} duplicate values, but should be unique",
+                 column=column,
+                 error_type="duplicate_values"
+             ))
+         
+         # Check for minimum value
+         if "minimum" in constraints:
+             min_value = constraints["minimum"]
+             if values.lt(min_value).any():
+                 invalid_count = values.lt(min_value).sum()
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Column '{column}' has {invalid_count} values less than minimum ({min_value})",
+                     column=column,
+                     error_type="minimum_violation"
+                 ))
+         
+         # Check for maximum value
+         if "maximum" in constraints:
+             max_value = constraints["maximum"]
+             if values.gt(max_value).any():
+                 invalid_count = values.gt(max_value).sum()
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Column '{column}' has {invalid_count} values greater than maximum ({max_value})",
+                     column=column,
+                     error_type="maximum_violation"
+                 ))
+         
+         # Check for pattern
+         if "pattern" in constraints and values.dtype == object:
+             pattern = constraints["pattern"]
+             try:
+                 import re
+                 regex = re.compile(pattern)
+                 invalid_mask = ~values.fillna("").str.match(regex)
+                 if invalid_mask.any():
+                     invalid_count = invalid_mask.sum()
+                     result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                         message=f"Column '{column}' has {invalid_count} values not matching pattern '{pattern}'",
+                         column=column,
+                         error_type="pattern_violation"
+                     ))
+             except Exception as e:
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Error validating pattern '{pattern}' for column '{column}': {str(e)}",
+                     column=column,
+                     severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                     error_type="pattern_error"
+                 ))
+         
+         # Check for enum values
+         if "enum" in constraints:
+             enum_values = set(constraints["enum"])
+             invalid_mask = ~values.isin(enum_values)
+             if invalid_mask.any():
+                 invalid_count = invalid_mask.sum()
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Column '{column}' has {invalid_count} values not in enum {enum_values}",
+                     column=column,
+                     error_type="enum_violation"
+                 ))
+     
+     def validate_constraints(self, data: pd.DataFrame, constraints: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> DataValidationResult:
+         """
+         Validate a DataFrame against a list of constraints.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to validate
+             constraints: The constraints to validate against
+                 Each constraint should be a dictionary with the following keys:
+                 - type: The type of constraint (e.g., "uniqueness", "relationship", "custom")
+                 - columns: The columns to validate
+                 - parameters: Additional parameters for the constraint
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Validation result
+         """
+         result = DataValidationResult()
+         
+         for constraint in constraints:
+             constraint_type = constraint.get("type")
+             columns = constraint.get("columns", [])
+             parameters = constraint.get("parameters", {})
+             
+             if not all(col in data.columns for col in columns):
+                 missing_columns = [col for col in columns if col not in data.columns]
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Constraint references missing columns: {', '.join(missing_columns)}",
+                     error_type="missing_columns"
+                 ))
+                 continue
+             
+             if constraint_type == "uniqueness":
+                 # Check if the combination of columns is unique
+                 if not data[columns].drop_duplicates().shape[0] == data.shape[0]:
+                     duplicate_count = data.shape[0] - data[columns].drop_duplicates().shape[0]
+                     result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                         message=f"Columns {columns} have {duplicate_count} duplicate combinations",
+                         error_type="uniqueness_violation"
+                     ))
+             
+             elif constraint_type == "relationship":
+                 # Check if values in one column depend on values in another column
+                 source_column = parameters.get("source_column")
+                 target_column = parameters.get("target_column")
+                 relationship = parameters.get("relationship", "one_to_one")
+                 
+                 if source_column not in data.columns or target_column not in data.columns:
+                     missing_columns = []
+                     if source_column not in data.columns:
+                         missing_columns.append(source_column)
+                     if target_column not in data.columns:
+                         missing_columns.append(target_column)
+                     
+                     result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                         message=f"Relationship constraint references missing columns: {', '.join(missing_columns)}",
+                         error_type="missing_columns"
+                     ))
+                     continue
+                 
+                 if relationship == "one_to_one":
+                     # Each value in source should map to exactly one value in target
+                     grouped = data.groupby(source_column)[target_column].nunique()
+                     invalid_sources = grouped[grouped > 1].index.tolist()
+                     
+                     if invalid_sources:
+                         result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                             message=f"One-to-one relationship violated: {len(invalid_sources)} source values map to multiple target values",
+                             details={"invalid_sources": invalid_sources[:10]},
+                             error_type="relationship_violation"
+                         ))
+                 
+                 elif relationship == "many_to_one":
+                     # Each value in target should have at least one value in source
+                     target_values = data[target_column].unique()
+                     source_values = data.groupby(target_column)[source_column].nunique().index.tolist()
+                     missing_targets = set(target_values) - set(source_values)
+                     
+                     if missing_targets:
+                         result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                             message=f"Many-to-one relationship violated: {len(missing_targets)} target values have no source values",
+                             details={"missing_targets": list(missing_targets)[:10]},
+                             error_type="relationship_violation"
+                         ))
+             
+             elif constraint_type == "custom":
+                 # Apply a custom validation function
+                 validation_function = parameters.get("function")
+                 if validation_function and callable(validation_function):
+                     try:
+                         custom_result = validation_function(data, columns, parameters)
+                         if isinstance(custom_result, bool):
+                             if not custom_result:
+                                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                                     message=f"Custom constraint failed for columns {columns}",
+                                     error_type="custom_constraint_violation"
+                                 ))
+                         elif isinstance(custom_result, DataValidationResult):
+                             result.merge(custom_result)
+                         else:
+                             result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                                 message=f"Custom constraint returned invalid result type: {type(custom_result)}",
+                                 severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                                 error_type="custom_constraint_error"
+                             ))
+                     except Exception as e:
+                         result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                             message=f"Error applying custom constraint: {str(e)}",
+                             severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                             error_type="custom_constraint_error"
+                         ))
+             
+             else:
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Unknown constraint type: {constraint_type}",
+                     severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                     error_type="unknown_constraint"
+                 ))
+         
+         return result
+     
+     def validate_integrity(self, data: pd.DataFrame, reference_data: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
+                          integrity_rules: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> DataValidationResult:
+         """
+         Validate the integrity of a DataFrame against reference data.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to validate
+             reference_data: Dictionary mapping reference names to reference DataFrames
+             integrity_rules: The integrity rules to validate against
+                 Each rule should be a dictionary with the following keys:
+                 - type: The type of integrity rule (e.g., "foreign_key", "check")
+                 - columns: The columns to validate
+                 - reference: The reference data to validate against
+                 - parameters: Additional parameters for the rule
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Validation result
+         """
+         result = DataValidationResult()
+         
+         for rule in integrity_rules:
+             rule_type = rule.get("type")
+             columns = rule.get("columns", [])
+             reference_name = rule.get("reference")
+             parameters = rule.get("parameters", {})
+             
+             if not all(col in data.columns for col in columns):
+                 missing_columns = [col for col in columns if col not in data.columns]
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Integrity rule references missing columns: {', '.join(missing_columns)}",
+                     error_type="missing_columns"
+                 ))
+                 continue
+             
+             if rule_type == "foreign_key":
+                 # Check if values in columns exist in reference data
+                 if reference_name not in reference_data:
+                     result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                         message=f"Reference data '{reference_name}' not found",
+                         error_type="missing_reference"
+                     ))
+                     continue
+                 
+                 reference_df = reference_data[reference_name]
+                 reference_columns = parameters.get("reference_columns", columns)
+                 
+                 if not all(col in reference_df.columns for col in reference_columns):
+                     missing_columns = [col for col in reference_columns if col not in reference_df.columns]
+                     result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                         message=f"Reference data '{reference_name}' missing columns: {', '.join(missing_columns)}",
+                         error_type="missing_reference_columns"
+                     ))
+                     continue
+                 
+                 # Check if all values in columns exist in reference_columns
+                 if len(columns) == 1 and len(reference_columns) == 1:
+                     # Simple case: single column
+                     col = columns[0]
+                     ref_col = reference_columns[0]
+                     
+                     invalid_values = set(data[col].dropna()) - set(reference_df[ref_col].dropna())
+                     if invalid_values:
+                         result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                             message=f"Foreign key violation: {len(invalid_values)} values in '{col}' not found in reference '{reference_name}.{ref_col}'",
+                             column=col,
+                             details={"invalid_values": list(invalid_values)[:10]},
+                             error_type="foreign_key_violation"
+                         ))
+                 else:
+                     # Complex case: multiple columns
+                     data_values = set(map(tuple, data[columns].dropna().values))
+                     reference_values = set(map(tuple, reference_df[reference_columns].dropna().values))
+                     
+                     invalid_values = data_values - reference_values
+                     if invalid_values:
+                         result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                             message=f"Foreign key violation: {len(invalid_values)} combinations in {columns} not found in reference '{reference_name}.{reference_columns}'",
+                             details={"invalid_values": [list(v) for v in list(invalid_values)[:10]]},
+                             error_type="foreign_key_violation"
+                         ))
+             
+             elif rule_type == "check":
+                 # Apply a check constraint
+                 check_expression = parameters.get("expression")
+                 if check_expression:
+                     try:
+                         # Evaluate the check expression
+                         check_result = eval(check_expression, {"data": data, "np": np, "pd": pd})
+                         if not check_result:
+                             result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                                 message=f"Check constraint failed: {check_expression}",
+                                 error_type="check_violation"
+                             ))
+                     except Exception as e:
+                         result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                             message=f"Error evaluating check constraint: {str(e)}",
+                             severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                             error_type="check_error"
+                         ))
+             
+             else:
+                 result.add_error(DataValidationError(
+                     message=f"Unknown integrity rule type: {rule_type}",
+                     severity=ValidationSeverity.WARNING,
+                     error_type="unknown_rule"
+                 ))
+         
+         return result
+ 
+ # Convenience functions
+ 
+ def validate_data_schema(data: pd.DataFrame, schema: Dict[str, Any]) -> DataValidationResult:
+     """
+     Validate a DataFrame against a schema.
+     
+     Args:
+         data: The DataFrame to validate
+         schema: The schema to validate against
+             
+     Returns:
+         Validation result
+     """
+     validator = DataValidator()
+     return validator.validate_schema(data, schema)
+ 
+ def validate_data_constraints(data: pd.DataFrame, constraints: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> DataValidationResult:
+     """
+     Validate a DataFrame against a list of constraints.
+     
+     Args:
+         data: The DataFrame to validate
+         constraints: The constraints to validate against
+             
+     Returns:
+         Validation result
+     """
+     validator = DataValidator()
+     return validator.validate_constraints(data, constraints)
+ 
+ def validate_data_integrity(data: pd.DataFrame, reference_data: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
+                           integrity_rules: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> DataValidationResult:
+     """
+     Validate the integrity of a DataFrame against reference data.
+     
+     Args:
+         data: The DataFrame to validate
+         reference_data: Dictionary mapping reference names to reference DataFrames
+         integrity_rules: The integrity rules to validate against
+             
+     Returns:
+         Validation result
+     """
+     validator = DataValidator()
+     return validator.validate_integrity(data, reference_data, integrity_rules)
```

```diff
+ """
+ Data Quality Metrics Module
+ 
+ This module provides tools for measuring and monitoring data quality metrics.
+ It helps quantify the quality of data across various dimensions such as completeness,
+ accuracy, consistency, timeliness, and uniqueness.
+ """
+ 
+ import pandas as pd
+ import numpy as np
+ import logging
+ from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union, Any, Tuple, Set, Callable
+ from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+ from enum import Enum
+ from dataclasses import dataclass
+ 
+ logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+ 
+ class MetricType(Enum):
+     """Types of data quality metrics."""
+     COMPLETENESS = "completeness"
+     ACCURACY = "accuracy"
+     CONSISTENCY = "consistency"
+     TIMELINESS = "timeliness"
+     UNIQUENESS = "uniqueness"
+     VALIDITY = "validity"
+     INTEGRITY = "integrity"
+     CUSTOM = "custom"
+ 
+ @dataclass
+ class DataQualityMetric:
+     """
+     Represents a data quality metric.
+     
+     Attributes:
+         name: Name of the metric
+         value: Numeric value of the metric
+         metric_type: Type of metric
+         description: Description of what the metric measures
+         timestamp: When the metric was calculated
+         column: Column the metric applies to (if applicable)
+         threshold: Threshold for acceptable values (if applicable)
+         is_passing: Whether the metric passes the threshold
+         details: Additional details about the metric
+     """
+     name: str
+     value: float
+     metric_type: MetricType
+     description: str
+     timestamp: datetime = None
+     column: Optional[str] = None
+     threshold: Optional[float] = None
+     is_passing: Optional[bool] = None
+     details: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
+     
+     def __post_init__(self):
+         """Initialize default values after creation."""
+         if self.timestamp is None:
+             self.timestamp = datetime.now()
+         
+         if self.threshold is not None and self.is_passing is None:
+             if self.metric_type in [MetricType.COMPLETENESS, MetricType.ACCURACY, 
+                                    MetricType.VALIDITY, MetricType.INTEGRITY]:
+                 # Higher is better for these metrics
+                 self.is_passing = self.value >= self.threshold
+             elif self.metric_type in [MetricType.CONSISTENCY, MetricType.TIMELINESS]:
+                 # Lower is better for these metrics
+                 self.is_passing = self.value <= self.threshold
+             else:
+                 # For other metrics, we can't determine automatically
+                 self.is_passing = None
+     
+     def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+         """
+         Convert the metric to a dictionary.
+         
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary representation of the metric
+         """
+         result = {
+             "name": self.name,
+             "value": self.value,
+             "metric_type": self.metric_type.value,
+             "description": self.description,
+             "timestamp": self.timestamp.isoformat()
+         }
+         
+         if self.column is not None:
+             result["column"] = self.column
+         
+         if self.threshold is not None:
+             result["threshold"] = self.threshold
+         
+         if self.is_passing is not None:
+             result["is_passing"] = self.is_passing
+         
+         if self.details is not None:
+             result["details"] = self.details
+         
+         return result
+ 
+ class DataQualityReport:
+     """
+     A collection of data quality metrics.
+     
+     Attributes:
+         metrics: List of data quality metrics
+         dataset_name: Name of the dataset
+         timestamp: When the report was created
+         overall_score: Overall data quality score
+     """
+     
+     def __init__(self, dataset_name: str):
+         """
+         Initialize a data quality report.
+         
+         Args:
+             dataset_name: Name of the dataset
+         """
+         self.metrics: List[DataQualityMetric] = []
+         self.dataset_name = dataset_name
+         self.timestamp = datetime.now()
+         self.overall_score: Optional[float] = None
+     
+     def add_metric(self, metric: DataQualityMetric) -> None:
+         """
+         Add a metric to the report.
+         
+         Args:
+             metric: The metric to add
+         """
+         self.metrics.append(metric)
+         self._recalculate_overall_score()
+     
+     def add_metrics(self, metrics: List[DataQualityMetric]) -> None:
+         """
+         Add multiple metrics to the report.
+         
+         Args:
+             metrics: The metrics to add
+         """
+         self.metrics.extend(metrics)
+         self._recalculate_overall_score()
+     
+     def _recalculate_overall_score(self) -> None:
+         """Recalculate the overall data quality score."""
+         if not self.metrics:
+             self.overall_score = None
+             return
+         
+         # Calculate weighted average of metrics
+         # We weight completeness and accuracy higher than other metrics
+         weights = {
+             MetricType.COMPLETENESS: 0.25,
+             MetricType.ACCURACY: 0.25,
+             MetricType.CONSISTENCY: 0.15,
+             MetricType.TIMELINESS: 0.10,
+             MetricType.UNIQUENESS: 0.10,
+             MetricType.VALIDITY: 0.15,
+             MetricType.INTEGRITY: 0.15,
+             MetricType.CUSTOM: 0.10
+         }
+         
+         total_weight = 0
+         weighted_sum = 0
+         
+         for metric in self.metrics:
+             # Skip metrics that don't contribute to overall score
+             if metric.metric_type == MetricType.CUSTOM and metric.details and not metric.details.get("include_in_overall", True):
+                 continue
+             
+             weight = weights.get(metric.metric_type, 0.1)
+             
+             # For metrics where lower is better, convert to a 0-1 scale where 1 is best
+             if metric.metric_type in [MetricType.CONSISTENCY, MetricType.TIMELINESS]:
+                 # Assuming these metrics are on a 0-1 scale
+                 value = 1 - metric.value
+             else:
+                 value = metric.value
+             
+             weighted_sum += value * weight
+             total_weight += weight
+         
+         if total_weight > 0:
+             self.overall_score = weighted_sum / total_weight
+         else:
+             self.overall_score = None
+     
+     def get_metrics_by_type(self, metric_type: MetricType) -> List[DataQualityMetric]:
+         """
+         Get metrics of a specific type.
+         
+         Args:
+             metric_type: The type of metrics to get
+             
+         Returns:
+             List of metrics of the specified type
+         """
+         return [m for m in self.metrics if m.metric_type == metric_type]
+     
+     def get_metrics_by_column(self, column: str) -> List[DataQualityMetric]:
+         """
+         Get metrics for a specific column.
+         
+         Args:
+             column: The column to get metrics for
+             
+         Returns:
+             List of metrics for the specified column
+         """
+         return [m for m in self.metrics if m.column == column]
+     
+     def get_failing_metrics(self) -> List[DataQualityMetric]:
+         """
+         Get metrics that fail their thresholds.
+         
+         Returns:
+             List of failing metrics
+         """
+         return [m for m in self.metrics if m.is_passing is not None and not m.is_passing]
+     
+     def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+         """
+         Convert the report to a dictionary.
+         
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary representation of the report
+         """
+         return {
+             "dataset_name": self.dataset_name,
+             "timestamp": self.timestamp.isoformat(),
+             "overall_score": self.overall_score,
+             "metrics": [m.to_dict() for m in self.metrics],
+             "metrics_count": len(self.metrics),
+             "failing_metrics_count": len(self.get_failing_metrics())
+         }
+     
+     def to_dataframe(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
+         """
+         Convert the report to a DataFrame.
+         
+         Returns:
+             DataFrame representation of the report
+         """
+         data = []
+         for metric in self.metrics:
+             row = {
+                 "name": metric.name,
+                 "value": metric.value,
+                 "metric_type": metric.metric_type.value,
+                 "description": metric.description,
+                 "timestamp": metric.timestamp,
+                 "column": metric.column,
+                 "threshold": metric.threshold,
+                 "is_passing": metric.is_passing
+             }
+             data.append(row)
+         
+         return pd.DataFrame(data)
+ 
+ class DataQualityMetrics:
+     """
+     Utility class for calculating data quality metrics.
+     """
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def completeness(data: pd.DataFrame, column: Optional[str] = None) -> Union[float, Dict[str, float]]:
+         """
+         Calculate completeness metric (percentage of non-null values).
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             column: Optional column to calculate completeness for
+                 If None, calculate for all columns
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Completeness metric (0-1 scale) for the specified column(s)
+         """
+         if column is not None:
+             if column not in data.columns:
+                 raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' not found in DataFrame")
+             return 1 - data[column].isna().mean()
+         else:
+             result = {}
+             for col in data.columns:
+                 result[col] = 1 - data[col].isna().mean()
+             return result
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def uniqueness(data: pd.DataFrame, column: Optional[str] = None) -> Union[float, Dict[str, float]]:
+         """
+         Calculate uniqueness metric (percentage of unique values).
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             column: Optional column to calculate uniqueness for
+                 If None, calculate for all columns
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Uniqueness metric (0-1 scale) for the specified column(s)
+         """
+         if column is not None:
+             if column not in data.columns:
+                 raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' not found in DataFrame")
+             return data[column].nunique() / len(data) if len(data) > 0 else 1.0
+         else:
+             result = {}
+             for col in data.columns:
+                 result[col] = data[col].nunique() / len(data) if len(data) > 0 else 1.0
+             return result
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def value_distribution(data: pd.DataFrame, column: str, bins: int = 10) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+         """
+         Calculate value distribution for a column.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             column: Column to calculate distribution for
+             bins: Number of bins for numeric columns
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary with value distribution information
+         """
+         if column not in data.columns:
+             raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' not found in DataFrame")
+         
+         column_data = data[column]
+         result = {
+             "count": len(column_data),
+             "missing_count": column_data.isna().sum(),
+             "missing_percentage": column_data.isna().mean() * 100
+         }
+         
+         if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(column_data):
+             # Numeric column
+             result.update({
+                 "min": column_data.min(),
+                 "max": column_data.max(),
+                 "mean": column_data.mean(),
+                 "median": column_data.median(),
+                 "std": column_data.std(),
+                 "histogram": np.histogram(column_data.dropna(), bins=bins)
+             })
+         elif pd.api.types.is_categorical_dtype(column_data) or pd.api.types.is_object_dtype(column_data):
+             # Categorical or string column
+             value_counts = column_data.value_counts(dropna=False)
+             result.update({
+                 "unique_count": column_data.nunique(),
+                 "top_values": value_counts.head(10).to_dict(),
+                 "top_values_percentage": (value_counts.head(10) / len(column_data) * 100).to_dict()
+             })
+         
+         return result
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def timeliness(data: pd.DataFrame, timestamp_column: str, 
+                  reference_time: Optional[datetime] = None,
+                  max_age: Optional[timedelta] = None) -> float:
+         """
+         Calculate timeliness metric (percentage of records that are recent).
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             timestamp_column: Column containing timestamps
+             reference_time: Reference time to compare against (default: current time)
+             max_age: Maximum acceptable age for records (default: 1 day)
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Timeliness metric (0-1 scale)
+         """
+         if timestamp_column not in data.columns:
+             raise ValueError(f"Column '{timestamp_column}' not found in DataFrame")
+         
+         if reference_time is None:
+             reference_time = datetime.now()
+         
+         if max_age is None:
+             max_age = timedelta(days=1)
+         
+         # Convert timestamp column to datetime if needed
+         timestamps = pd.to_datetime(data[timestamp_column])
+         
+         # Calculate age of each record
+         ages = reference_time - timestamps
+         
+         # Calculate percentage of records within acceptable age
+         return (ages <= max_age).mean()
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def accuracy(data: pd.DataFrame, column: str, reference_data: pd.DataFrame, 
+                reference_column: Optional[str] = None) -> float:
+         """
+         Calculate accuracy metric (percentage of values that match reference data).
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             column: Column to check accuracy for
+             reference_data: Reference DataFrame with correct values
+             reference_column: Column in reference data to compare against (default: same as column)
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Accuracy metric (0-1 scale)
+         """
+         if column not in data.columns:
+             raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' not found in DataFrame")
+         
+         if reference_column is None:
+             reference_column = column
+         
+         if reference_column not in reference_data.columns:
+             raise ValueError(f"Column '{reference_column}' not found in reference DataFrame")
+         
+         # Get values from both DataFrames
+         values = data[column]
+         reference_values = reference_data[reference_column]
+         
+         # Check if values match reference values
+         # This assumes the DataFrames have the same index or can be aligned
+         try:
+             matches = values == reference_values
+             return matches.mean()
+         except:
+             # If DataFrames can't be aligned, compare sets of values
+             values_set = set(values.dropna())
+             reference_set = set(reference_values.dropna())
+             
+             if not reference_set:
+                 return 0.0
+             
+             # Calculate Jaccard similarity
+             intersection = values_set.intersection(reference_set)
+             union = values_set.union(reference_set)
+             
+             return len(intersection) / len(union) if union else 1.0
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def consistency(data: pd.DataFrame, rules: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, float]:
+         """
+         Calculate consistency metric (percentage of records that satisfy consistency rules).
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             rules: List of consistency rules to check
+                 Each rule should be a dictionary with:
+                 - columns: List of columns involved in the rule
+                 - condition: String expression that should evaluate to True for consistent records
+                 - name: Name of the rule
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary mapping rule names to consistency metrics (0-1 scale)
+         """
+         result = {}
+         
+         for rule in rules:
+             columns = rule.get("columns", [])
+             condition = rule.get("condition")
+             name = rule.get("name", f"Rule for {', '.join(columns)}")
+             
+             if not all(col in data.columns for col in columns):
+                 missing_columns = [col for col in columns if col not in data.columns]
+                 logger.warning(f"Consistency rule '{name}' references missing columns: {missing_columns}")
+                 result[name] = 0.0
+                 continue
+             
+             if not condition:
+                 logger.warning(f"Consistency rule '{name}' has no condition")
+                 result[name] = 0.0
+                 continue
+             
+             try:
+                 # Evaluate the condition
+                 mask = eval(condition, {"data": data, "np": np, "pd": pd})
+                 consistency = mask.mean()
+                 result[name] = consistency
+             except Exception as e:
+                 logger.error(f"Error evaluating consistency rule '{name}': {str(e)}")
+                 result[name] = 0.0
+         
+         return result
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def validity(data: pd.DataFrame, column: str, validation_func: Callable[[Any], bool]) -> float:
+         """
+         Calculate validity metric (percentage of values that pass a validation function).
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             column: Column to check validity for
+             validation_func: Function that returns True for valid values
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Validity metric (0-1 scale)
+         """
+         if column not in data.columns:
+             raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' not found in DataFrame")
+         
+         # Apply validation function to each value
+         valid_mask = data[column].apply(lambda x: validation_func(x) if pd.notna(x) else False)
+         
+         return valid_mask.mean()
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def outlier_percentage(data: pd.DataFrame, column: str, method: str = "zscore", 
+                          threshold: float = 3.0) -> float:
+         """
+         Calculate percentage of outliers in a column.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             column: Column to check for outliers
+             method: Method to detect outliers ("zscore", "iqr", or "percentile")
+             threshold: Threshold for outlier detection
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Percentage of outliers (0-1 scale)
+         """
+         if column not in data.columns:
+             raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' not found in DataFrame")
+         
+         if not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[column]):
+             raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' is not numeric")
+         
+         values = data[column].dropna()
+         
+         if method == "zscore":
+             # Z-score method
+             mean = values.mean()
+             std = values.std()
+             if std == 0:
+                 return 0.0
+             z_scores = np.abs((values - mean) / std)
+             outliers = z_scores > threshold
+         elif method == "iqr":
+             # IQR method
+             q1 = values.quantile(0.25)
+             q3 = values.quantile(0.75)
+             iqr = q3 - q1
+             lower_bound = q1 - threshold * iqr
+             upper_bound = q3 + threshold * iqr
+             outliers = (values < lower_bound) | (values > upper_bound)
+         elif method == "percentile":
+             # Percentile method
+             lower_bound = values.quantile(threshold / 100)
+             upper_bound = values.quantile(1 - threshold / 100)
+             outliers = (values < lower_bound) | (values > upper_bound)
+         else:
+             raise ValueError(f"Unknown outlier detection method: {method}")
+         
+         return outliers.mean()
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def create_data_quality_report(data: pd.DataFrame, dataset_name: str) -> DataQualityReport:
+         """
+         Create a comprehensive data quality report for a DataFrame.
+         
+         Args:
+             data: The DataFrame to analyze
+             dataset_name: Name of the dataset
+                 
+         Returns:
+             Data quality report
+         """
+         report = DataQualityReport(dataset_name)
+         
+         # Calculate completeness for each column
+         completeness_metrics = DataQualityMetrics.completeness(data)
+         for column, value in completeness_metrics.items():
+             report.add_metric(DataQualityMetric(
+                 name=f"Completeness of {column}",
+                 value=value,
+                 metric_type=MetricType.COMPLETENESS,
+                 description=f"Percentage of non-null values in column {column}",
+                 column=column,
+                 threshold=0.95,  # 95% completeness threshold
+                 details={"missing_count": data[column].isna().sum()}
+             ))
+         
+         # Calculate uniqueness for each column
+         uniqueness_metrics = DataQualityMetrics.uniqueness(data)
+         for column, value in uniqueness_metrics.items():
+             report.add_metric(DataQualityMetric(
+                 name=f"Uniqueness of {column}",
+                 value=value,
+                 metric_type=MetricType.UNIQUENESS,
+                 description=f"Percentage of unique values in column {column}",
+                 column=column,
+                 details={"unique_count": data[column].nunique()}
+             ))
+         
+         # Calculate outlier percentage for numeric columns
+         for column in data.select_dtypes(include=np.number).columns:
+             try:
+                 outlier_pct = DataQualityMetrics.outlier_percentage(data, column)
+                 report.add_metric(DataQualityMetric(
+                     name=f"Outlier percentage of {column}",
+                     value=outlier_pct,
+                     metric_type=MetricType.VALIDITY,
+                     description=f"Percentage of outliers in column {column}",
+                     column=column,
+                     threshold=0.05,  # 5% outliers threshold
+                     details={"method": "zscore", "threshold": 3.0}
+                 ))
+             except Exception as e:
+                 logger.warning(f"Error calculating outliers for column {column}: {str(e)}")
+         
+         # Add overall completeness metric
+         overall_completeness = np.mean(list(completeness_metrics.values()))
+         report.add_metric(DataQualityMetric(
+             name="Overall completeness",
+             value=overall_completeness,
+             metric_type=MetricType.COMPLETENESS,
+             description="Average completeness across all columns",
+             threshold=0.95
+         ))
+         
+         return report
+ 
+ # Convenience functions
+ 
+ def calculate_completeness(data: pd.DataFrame, column: Optional[str] = None) -> Union[float, Dict[str, float]]:
+     """
+     Calculate completeness metric (percentage of non-null values).
+     
+     Args:
+         data: The DataFrame to analyze
+         column: Optional column to calculate completeness for
+             
+     Returns:
+         Completeness metric (0-1 scale) for the specified column(s)
+     """
+     return DataQualityMetrics.completeness(data, column)
+ 
+ def calculate_uniqueness(data: pd.DataFrame, column: Optional[str] = None) -> Union[float, Dict[str, float]]:
+     """
+     Calculate uniqueness metric (percentage of unique values).
+     
+     Args:
+         data: The DataFrame to analyze
+         column: Optional column to calculate uniqueness for
+             
+     Returns:
+         Uniqueness metric (0-1 scale) for the specified column(s)
+     """
+     return DataQualityMetrics.uniqueness(data, column)
+ 
+ def create_quality_report(data: pd.DataFrame, dataset_name: str) -> DataQualityReport:
+     """
+     Create a comprehensive data quality report for a DataFrame.
+     
+     Args:
+         data: The DataFrame to analyze
+         dataset_name: Name of the dataset
+             
+     Returns:
+         Data quality report
+     """
+     return DataQualityMetrics.create_data_quality_report(data, dataset_name)
```

```diff
+ """

+ class AnomalyDetector:
```
